paragraphs.source_en: I remember the sunrise over the sea of Fusang, gold spread across the sea of Fusang; I remember the islands on the sea of Fusang, emerald islets drifting upon it— Shayangnara! Passing through the light ripples, slow and gentle, I saw a tiny, old-fashioned fishing boat, like a flock of carefree seabirds, resting and drifting in the dusk shimmer of the waves, Shayangnara! This is a graveyard; Whose graveyard is it, that takes for itself the pure wind of these hills, the scent of pines and drifting clouds? I remember most vividly the beautiful tombstones and their inscriptions, the dead there had in life a clarity as clean as peaks and pine-scent— Shayangnara! 〈 （Kobe Mountain Cemetery） 〉 Hearing the nightingale-like song in the windward hollow, watching hawks with wide wings cross drifting clouds, I rest my eyes against an old pine: I ask whether those in the grave are as carefree as those above. —— Shayangnara! 〈 （Kobe Mountain Cemetery） 〉 Health, joy, wildness—madness— I envy you; you cry out together in one voice, “Aroya-jie!” I am glad to be part of this city’s rain of blossoms, a flock of butterflies taking wing in swift swarms, “Aroya-jie”! Shayangnara! 〈 （Osaka Festival） 〉 Add music to my dream—right here, now— a clatter of wooden sandals, crisp, fresh, and eager, with splendid lantern light filling every street, laughter rising in that glow, “Aroya-jie”! Shayangnara! 〈 （Osaka Festival） 〉 As if the elegance of the Three Gorges were carried on the wind, the Katsu River has continuous green cliffs like brocade; As if in the ravines one saw danger itself, a narrow skiff rushing through spray and foam— Shayangnara! 〈 （Rapid waters on the Katsu River） 〉 We cleared one gate of rapids, drifted through a stretch of clear ripples, and in those ripples there shone the dear image of green hills; Planting the long pole firmly, I anchored for a while in the heart of the waves, and in the wave-center watched a relaxed cluster of fish— Shayangnara! 〈 （same as above） 〉 Quiet! Let that clinging sound of oars fall still, listen to the ringing joy from the green woods, is it the blackbird, or the cuckoo? Like drops of perfume, dropping into my weary spirit, parched and longing— Shayangnara! 〈 （same as above） 〉 “Uta”: do not mock the visitors’ frenzy. Boatmen, you have already drunk the quiet grace of the waters and hills. Take a cup of “Shaji,” friends—let us all be drunk on the scenery, “Uta, Uta”! Even the mountain spirit does not disdain a rough, unpolished singing throat— Shayangnara! 〈 （same as above） 〉 I do not parse—there is no need to parse— the strange lyrics, like unruly waves growling in a rock cave, like an old samurai speaking of his life in his prime, “Uta Uta”! My heart is filled with radiant, wandering thoughts— Shayangnara! 〈 （same as above） 〉 That is the cuckoo! She embroiders a silk sash, gently trailing it along the green feet of the hills; Ah, in that blue water too, her trace of fragrance is there; in the blue water lies hidden her peach-bud-like shy beauty— Shayangnara! And yet it gives me deep, engulfing intoxication, not from the cuckoo flower’s own shy fragrance alone; Beyond the sweetness of the cuckoo, even sweeter still the maiden, more tender than gentleness itself—unforgettable. Shayangnara! I admire the lightness of their figures. Grace is innate—grace is inborn. I admire the evenness of their color, a butterfly-like brilliance, butterfly-like lightness— Shayangnara! They do not waste the maker’s craft, and in their sidelong glances there is endless attentiveness. Like the freedom of warm wind and flower-scent, I can never fully consume their smiles and tenderness. I am a night-butterfly from a secluded valley: taking form among grasses, flying in the dark, I offer the beautiful golden dust upon my wings, I adore stars far away across ten thousand miles— Shayangnara! I am a drunken flower-bee: I have sipped fully of fragrance and do not hide my wildness; now, on the way home, I hum with a small voice, wishing to praise another wine-like bloom I once drank deep of— Shayangnara! Most of all, that gentle bending of the head, like a water-lily too shy to bear the cool breeze; a tender farewell, a careful farewell, and in that one farewell is a honey-sweet sorrow— Shayangnara!

paragraphs.source_zh:
我記得扶桑海上的朝陽，

黃金似的散佈在扶桑的海上；

我記得扶桑海上的群島，

翡翠似的浮漚在扶桑的海上——

沙揚娜拉！

趁航在輕濤間，悠悠的，

我見有一星星古式的漁舟，

像一群無憂的海鳥，

在黃昏的波光裡息羽優游，

沙揚娜拉！

這是一座墓園；誰家的墓園

佔盡這山中的清風，松馨與留雲？

我最不忘那美麗的墓碑與碑銘，

墓中人生前亦有與山峰與松馨似的清明——

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（神戶山中墓園）
〉

聽見折風前的流鶯，

看闊翅的鷹鷂穿度浮雲，

我依著一本古松瞑眸：

問墓中人何似墓上人的清閒？ ——

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（神戶山中墓園）
〉

健康，歡欣，瘋魔，我羨慕，

你們同聲的歡呼“阿羅呀喈”！

我欣幸我參與著滿城的花雨，

連翩的蝴蝶飛舞，“阿羅呀喈”！

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（大阪慶典）
〉

增添我夢裡的音樂——便如今——

一聲聲的木屐，清脆，新鮮，殷勤，

有況是滿街艷麗的燈影，

燈影裡歡聲騰越，“阿羅呀喈”！

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（大阪慶典）
〉

彷彿三峽間的風流，

保津川有青嶂連綿的錦繡；

彷彿山峽見的險巇

飛沫裡趁急失似的扁舟—

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（保津川急湍）
〉

廢一關湍險，駛一段清漣，

清漣裡有青山的倩影；

撐定了長篙，小駐在波心，

波心裡看閒適的魚群——

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（同前）
〉

靜！且停那槳聲膠愛，

聽青林裡嘹亮的歡欣，

是畫眉，是知更？像是滴滴的香液，

滴入我的苦渴的心靈——

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（同前）
〉

“烏塔”：莫訕笑遊客的瘋狂，

舟人，你們享盡山水的清幽，

喝一杯“沙雞”，朋友，共醉風光，

“烏塔，烏塔”！山靈不嫌粗魯的歌喉——

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（同前）
〉

我不辨——辯亦無須——著異樣的歌詞，

像不逞的波瀾在岩窟見吽嘶，

像衰老的武士訴說壯年時的身世，

“烏塔烏塔”！我滿懷灩灩的遐思——

沙揚娜拉！
〈
（同前）
〉

那是杜鵑！她繡一條錦帶，

迤儷著那青山的青麓；

啊，那碧波里亦與她的芳躅，

碧波里那掩映著她桃蕊似的嬌怯——

沙揚娜拉！

但供給我沉酣的陶醉，

不僅是杜鵑花的幽芳；

倍勝於嬌柔的杜鵑，

最難忘更嬌柔的女郎！

沙揚娜拉！

我愛慕她們體態的輕盈，

嫵媚是天生，嫵媚是天生！

我愛慕她們顏色的調勻，

蝴蝶似的光艷，蝴蝶似的輕盈——

沙揚娜拉！

不辜負造物主的匠心，

她們流眄中有無限的殷勤；

比如熏風與花香似的自由，

我餐不盡她們的笑靨與柔情——

沙揚娜拉！

我是一隻幽谷裡的夜蝶：

在草叢間成形，在黑暗裡飛行，

我獻致我翅上美麗的金粉，

我愛戀萬萬里外的明星——

沙揚娜拉！

我是一隻酣醉了的花蜂：

我飽啜了芬芳，我不諱我的猖狂：

如今，在歸途上嚶嗡著小嗓，

想讚美那別樣的花釀，我曾經恣嘗——

沙揚娜拉！

最是那一低頭的溫柔，

像一朵水蓮花不勝涼風的嬌羞，

道一聲珍重，道一聲珍重，

那一聲珍重裡有蜜甜的憂愁——

沙揚娜拉！
